text:
Jordan: Heads-up — we just hit a sustained spike in external function invocations and structured-output payloads. GPU queues are ballooning and tail latency is >500ms for the last 6m. SLO alerts triggered.

incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — high fn-invoke/structured-output rate spike affecting hosted inference (severity: P1). Pager auto-notified eng-platform and eng-sre.

Jordan: I'm going to take an immediate mitigation: restrict structured output and non-essential external function calls for public-hosted traffic only. This should reduce KV-cache pressure and cut per-request work.

Priya: Agreed. Can we do a tiered restriction? Enterprise tenants (dedicated/private) should be untouched unless they opt into the restriction. We should keep streaming/text-only for now.

Mateo: Plan: 1) Feature-flag structured_output -> "restricted" for scope=public-hosted 2) Enforce per-tenant fn-invoke qps cap at 0.5 for best-effort tenants 3) Route non-critical requests to the cheaper small-model fallback to free up big GPUs.

Jordan: I have the admin toggle ready. Running the toggle now.

Jordan: ```
# admin API to restrict structured outputs for public-hosted
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/feature_flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"feature":"structured_output","state":"restricted","scope":"public-hosted","note":"mitigation: spike 2100001234"}'
```

deploy-bot: feature_flag structured_output -> restricted (public-hosted) by jordan — rollout started.

Jordan: Also applying a temporary per-tenant throttle:

Jordan: ```
# per-tenant throttle patch
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/quotas/bulk_update" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filter":"tenant_type:best_effort","quota":{"fn_invoke_qps":0.5,"structured_output_enabled":false}}'
```

Priya: Monitoring the queues now. Early signs: pod CPU for the big-gpu pool dropping ~20% and request queuing time cut in half. Latency trending down but still above SLO for a few customers.

Alexis: Support — calling out two hosted customers with high fn-invoke traffic (acct-827 and acct-129). Will open incident notes and draft an advisory. Do we want to message them now or wait for stability?

Jordan: Draft message ok. Keep it factual and say we are restricting structured output and function call capacity to protect stability; we're prioritizing dedicated customers and will update in 30m. Alexis, add suggested ETA for re-evaluation at +30m.

Alexis: On it. I'll paste the draft here for review in a sec.

Mateo: One more safeguard: increase fallback probability to small-model by 60% for public-hosted routing policy so fewer requests hit the large-model queue. Command below.

Mateo: ```
# adjust routing weights (public-hosted): favor small model
curl -X POST "https://router.api.internal/redwood/v1/routing_weights" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"public-hosted","policy":"prefer_small","weight_delta":0.6,"reason":"reduce big-gpu load"}'
```

Priya: Nice. I'm watching task latencies and backend error rates. If p95 drops below 300ms we'll consider partial re-enable.

Jordan: Current status update: structured_output restricted (public-hosted) — active. Per-tenant throttle applied. Routing weights adjusted.

incident-bot: UPDATE — mitigation actions applied by Jordan and Mateo. Please keep comments / new actions in the thread. Next automated check in 5m.

Priya: Observability note — enable verbose KV-cache metrics in the console so we can see hit/miss ratio as we run the restriction. Mateo, can you flip that?

Mateo: Done — KV cache diagnostics enabled on the affected pools. Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-cache/kv-diagnostics?orgId=1

Jordan: Quick check on customer impact: support reports that acct-827 saw degraded structured JSON responses -> now returns text-only with a short note about disabled structured output. acct-129 had retries but no errors. No enterprise SLAs impacted.

Alexis: Draft advisory for hosted customers: "We're temporarily restricting structured outputs and external function invocation for hosted tiers to protect service stability. You may receive text-only responses until normal operations resume. We're prioritizing Dedicated and Private customers. We'll update within 30 minutes." Any edits?

Priya: Add: "If you believe your workload requires exempting, open a support ticket referencing incident 2100001234."

Alexis: Updated and queued to send to affected tenants.

Jordan: Handoff — I'm scheduled to head offline at 03:00 UTC. Priya, can you take lead for the next hour? We'll do a formal handoff with checklist: current mitigations, metrics to watch (p95 latency, gpu-queue-length, fn_invoke_rate), and customer list.

Priya: Taking lead. I'll monitor and keep this thread as the single source of truth. If we see reversion conditions (p95 < 300ms and fn_invoke_rate stable for 10m) we'll gradually re-enable structured_output for public-hosted in a canary of 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

Jordan: Thanks. I'll note the actions in the incident tracker and tag follow-ups: runbook gaps (need a dedicated play for tiered restrictions), and automation (automate toggle based on queue length).

deploy-bot: Incident 2100001234 annotated: mitigation_by_human (structured_output_restriction, fn_quota_patch, routing_adjust).

Priya: Quick update at +27m: p95 = 280ms, gpu-queue-length stable, fn_invoke_rate down 72% for public-hosted. I'm starting canary: structured_output -> limited for 5% traffic.

Mateo: Canary command: ```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/feature_flags/canary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"feature":"structured_output","scope":"public-hosted","canary_pct":5}'
```

Priya: Canary live. Monitoring.

Alexis: Notifying affected hosts that we're testing partial restore; email queued.

Priya: Canary looking good for 12 minutes. Increasing to 25%.

Jordan: Back briefly — great work. If all green at 25% for 15m, proceed to 100%. Make sure we keep the per-tenant qps caps until 100% is proven stable for 30m.

Priya: Understood. Will only remove the per-tenant throttle after 30m of stable at 100%.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — mitigations successful and services restored to normal; final note: structured_output restored 100% after progressive canary. Closing incident 2100001234.

Jordan: Marking follow-ups: automation playbook, customer comm retrospective, and a postmortem action item for better signal thresholds. Thanks everyone — big help.

Alexis: Drafted post-incident email for affected hosted tenants. Will circulate for review.

Priya: Handing off monitoring to Mateo for the next 2 hours. I'll stay available for pager.

Mateo: Acknowledged.

Jordan: Signed off.
